articles.title: Federal appeals court gives President Donald Trump path to erasing hush money conviction
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The panel ordered a lower court to promptly issue a decision on whether the case should remain in federal court; if that happens, Mr. Trump could then argue that the verdict should be discarded because of Presidential immunity

A federal appeals court on Monday (November 23, 2026) gave U.S. President Donald Trump a new pathway to erasing his hush money criminal conviction, moving the case to a federal court where he could seek to have it dismissed on immunity grounds.

A three-judge panel of the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court decision that had kept the case in state court in New York, where Mr. Trump was tried and convicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to obscure a $130,000 payment to adult film performer Stormy Daniels.

The panel ordered a lower court to promptly issue a decision on whether the case should remain in federal court. If that happens, Mr. Trump could then argue that the verdict should be discarded because of Presidential immunity.

The decision also set in motion a halt to proceedings in Mr. Trump's simultaneous state court appeal. Trump denies wrongdoing and was given no punishment in the case, which made him the first U.S. President convicted of a crime.

In a two-page order, the 2nd Circuit panel said it disagreed with the late US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein's earlier denial of Mr. Trump's request to move the historic case from state court to federal court, a process known as removal.

articles.title: Bisleri controversy: Goa FDA steps up surveillance of packaged water brands
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: FDA Director Shweta S. Dessai said the disputed Bisleri batch was tested in October 2025 and was no longer available in the market

Goa's Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) has intensified surveillance of packaged drinking water brands sold in theSstate following a controversy over a Bisleri sample declared unsafe, a senior official said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

FDA Director Shweta S. Dessai said the disputed Bisleri batch was tested in October 2025 and was no longer available in the market, adding that the Food Safety Officer (FSO) has filed a prosecution case in court in connection with the sample.

"This particular batch is not available in the market. However, I have instructed my officers to draw surveillance samples of various packaged drinking water brands) manufactured and sold in Goa for analysis," Ms. Dessai said.
She said that from April 1, 2025, till date, the FDA had analysed more than 80 samples of packaged drinking water as part of its quality surveillance exercise.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) on Sunday (November 22) said it had sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International Pvt Ltd over "unsafe packaged drinking water" from its Goa manufacturing facility.
ALSO WATCH Watch: Bisleri faces prosecution after FSSAI finds water sample ‘unsafe’
Bisleri, meanwhile, has maintained that its packaged drinking water is safe for consumption, stating that the issue relates to a single batch manufactured at its Goa facility in September 2025.

On September 30, 2025, FSSAI collected six samples from the Goa facility, and initial testing found that five met all applicable standards, the company said. "The sixth recorded a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre," it stated.
In a statement, the company said it had not received any notice from the FSSAI, adding that a referral laboratory had found bromate levels within the prescribed limit.
Bisleri said it would continue to cooperate with the FSSAI to address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process.

fullParagraphs: The State government should immediately intervene and take action ensuring that the woman district Collector gets justice
TNCC president, B. Manickam Tagore, has demanded immediate registration of case under relevant sections against Kallakurichi TVK MLA, Arul Vignesh, and initiation of legal action without any delay.

Expressing shock over the report of ‘ The Hindu’ over the Kallakurichi District Collector, having lodged a police complaint over the TVK MLA on charges of having sent “obscene” messages to her, the Congress MP sought immediate action against Arul Vignesh.
“As the affected woman officer herself has lodged the complaint, immediate action should be taken against the MLA,” he said in a social media post.

Mr. Tagore also said that it was the duty of the government to ensure dignity and protection to the woman officer at the helm of administration, he said. “No one should get any exemption from the legal action just because he or she was in power,” the Virudhunagar MP said.
The State government should immediately intervene and take action ensuring that the woman district Collector gets justice.

articles.title: Collector files complaint against Kallakurichi TVK MLA
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: It is learnt that the Collector had accused the MLA of having made inappropriate advances and sent unwarranted messages
The Kallakurichi Collector handed over a formal complaint to the Superintendent of Police against Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam MLA C. Arul Vignesh, sources said on Monday afternoon (November 23, 2026).

It is learnt that the Collector had accused the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages. The police are learnt to have registered the complaint against the MLA under the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act. Senior police officers could not be reached for comment.

During the day, State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan told the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from the IAS officer. He gave an emphatic “no” in response to questions from Justice V. Lakshminarayanan as to whether the police or the Chief Secretary had received any complaint.
Then, the judge asked the SPP to get instructions from the officer and report to the court by Tuesday.

The court was hearing a writ petition (criminal), filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, seeking a direction to the police to file a criminal case against the MLA on the petitioner’s complaint that he had trespassed into the officer’s bungalow in an inebriated state and threatened the officials there, besides sending the officer obscene messages.

When the judge wanted to know how the petitioner knew about the alleged obscene messages, her counsel S. Jeyakumar replied that the woman officer had complained to the Chief Secretary. On being asked to place the complaint before the court, the counsel said, “It is not available with me, I agree.” He, however, accused the official respondents of suppressing the facts of the case.

“Everything is available with them but they are suppressing all those things. They are sailing with the accused and not at all taking care of the law. All higher officers are protecting the accused. In these circumstances, what will the...[woman IAS officer] do MiLord?” the counsel said. Surprised at his answer, the judge asked, “You mean to say that an IAS officer does not know how to protect herself?”

The judge also referred to the 2021 sexual harassment complaint filed by a woman IPS officer against the then special DGP and said, “Last time when a similar incident happened, it was the woman officer who gave the complaint. Where is the complaint in the present instance? Are you and I going to do something that an IAS officer does not know...? She is the head of a district, I say.”

On being told by the petitioner’s counsel that the National Commission for Women (NCW) had taken suo motu cognisance of the issue on the basis of newspaper reports and called for a report from the DGP, the judge said, “They can act based on newspaper reports, I cannot. Give me some tangible material to show that the MLA had, indeed, sent obscene messages and I will issue a (writ of) mandamus.”

Stating that the petitioner appeared to be trying to fish in troubled waters, Justice Lakshminarayanan also said, “If the officer concerned has not made any complaint, where is the question of the police taking action? Do you want them [the police] to take action on the basis of newspaper reports? If there is no complaint by the woman, I will not interfere.”

articles.title: Invoking Bengal famine, India tells UNSC costs of conflict not shared equally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, told a high-level briefing of the Security Council that developing countries were bearing the brunt of food, fuel, fertiliser and energy shortages caused by global conflicts

India has invoked the 1943 Bengal famine at the UN Security Council to highlight the disproportionate impact of conflicts on the Global South , calling for measures to prevent food insecurity amid the Ukraine war.

India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, told a high-level briefing of the Security Council on Monday (November 23, 2026) that developing countries were bearing the brunt of food, fuel, fertiliser and energy shortages caused by global conflicts.
“India has consistently emphasised that the costs of conflict are not shared equally,” he said.
“Global South countries are the most adversely affected by the food, fuel, and fertiliser crisis caused by today's global conflicts,” he added.

Invoking the Bengal famine , which killed over three million people, Mr. Parvathaneni said it was a reminder of the “terrible human cost” of a distant conflict caused by unchecked wartime priorities and calculations.

Addressing the briefing on 'Protecting critical energy infrastructure and Black Sea lifelines of global food supply', Mr. Parvathaneni said that in an interconnected world, the implications of the Ukraine conflict, now in its fifth year, were being felt everywhere.

Recalling Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s message that the world has to move from endless war to the end of war, he reiterated India's readiness to contribute to all efforts towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict.
He also stressed that Mr. Modi was firmly on the side of the Global South when he said that “this is not an era of war.”
India noted with concern that conflicts exacerbate food insecurity by disrupting agriculture, displacing communities, damaging infrastructure and hindering humanitarian access.
Their consequences extend globally through disruptions to energy, fertiliser supplies, transport and agricultural trade, disproportionately affecting the Global South.

Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, told a high-level briefing of the Security Council that developing countries were bearing the brunt of food, fuel, fertiliser and energy shortages caused by global conflicts

India has invoked the 1943 Bengal famine at the UN Security Council to highlight the disproportionate impact of conflicts on the Global South , calling for measures to prevent food insecurity amid the Ukraine war.

India’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, told a high-level briefing of the Security Council on Monday (November 23, 2026) that developing countries were bearing the brunt of food, fuel, fertiliser and energy shortages caused by global conflicts.

“India has consistently emphasised that the costs of conflict are not shared equally,” he said.

“Global South countries are the most adversely affected by the food, fuel, and fertiliser crisis caused by today's global conflicts,” he added.

Invoking the Bengal famine , which killed over three million people, Mr. Parvathaneni said it was a reminder of the “terrible human cost” of a distant conflict caused by unchecked wartime priorities and calculations.

Addressing the briefing on 'Protecting critical energy infrastructure and Black Sea lifelines of global food supply', Mr. Parvathaneni said that in an interconnected world, the implications of the Ukraine conflict, now in its fifth year, were being felt everywhere.

Recalling Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s message that the world has to move from endless war to the end of war, he reiterated India's readiness to contribute to all efforts towards a peaceful resolution of the conflict.

He also stressed that Mr. Modi was firmly on the side of the Global South when he said that “this is not an era of war.”

India noted with concern that conflicts exacerbate food insecurity by disrupting agriculture, displacing communities, damaging infrastructure and hindering humanitarian access.

Their consequences extend globally through disruptions to energy, fertiliser supplies, transport and agricultural trade, disproportionately affecting the Global South.

articles.title: Stalin urges Tamil Nadu government to act against Kallakurichi TVK MLA over messages to Collector
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The incident raised questions about what would happen to an ordinary woman if a Collector herself faced such a situation, Mr. Stalin said

DMK president M.K. Stalin on Tuesday (November 24*, 2026) urged the Tamil Nadu government to take action against Kallakurichi MLA Arul Vignesh over allegations that he had sent inappropriate messages to the district Collector.

Reacting to The Hindu report, “ Collector files complaint against Kallakurichi TVK MLA ”, Mr. Stalin said the Chief Minister and the Chief Secretary should have spoken to the Collector and assured her of support when reports about the inappropriate messages emerged several weeks ago.

“They should have condemned the MLA and taken action against him. Any government concerned about the welfare and safety of women would have done so. Since the government sought to protect its party MLA and its minority government, there was a delay in the woman Collector filing the complaint,” he said.
The incident raised questions about what would happen to an ordinary woman if a Collector herself faced such a situation, Mr. Stalin said.

“What is shameful is that some leaders aspiring for positions stood by the MLA instead of extending support to the Collector. It is highly condemnable that the government failed to act even though the issue was brought to its notice several times,” he alleged.
Mr. Stalin also claimed that the incident lent credence to allegations that TVK functionaries were involved in sexual offences and drug smuggling.

articles.title: Sheikh Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh from exile on Dec. 16

fullParagraphs: Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule

Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina plans to return home from exile in India on December 16, the day the country celebrates as Victory Day when it won independence after a war with Pakistan.
Ms. Hasina went into exile in India on August 5, 2024, after a student-led mass uprising forced her to end her 15-year rule.
In the statement on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) announcing the planned date of her return, she urged current Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline.

“Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali said in the statement.

articles.title: China's Shenzhou-24 spaceship to include first foreign astronaut from Pakistan
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Pakistani payload specialist Zeeshan Ali's participation is ‌part of bilateral cooperation under Beijing’s ‌Belt ⁠and Road Initiative

China will launch its Shenzhou-24 spaceship on Wednesday at ​8:18 a.m. local time (November 25) with a ‌crew including a Pakistani national, who ​will be the first foreign astronaut ⁠to board China’s space station.

The three-person flight crew consists of commander Tang Hongbo, flight engineer ‌Wu Yi and Pakistani payload specialist Zeeshan Ali, whose participation is ‌part of bilateral cooperation under Beijing’s ‌ Belt ⁠and Road Initiative.
The China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) announced on Tuesday that the crew ⁠is in good condition and launch preparations are complete.

​China’s Shenzhou missions ‌have sent trios of Chinese astronauts to the Tiangong station for six-month stays since 2021. Ali is scheduled for a ‌short-term visit before returning with two ​of the outgoing Shenzhou-23 crew.
People walk past a painting following a press conference before the Shenzhou-24 spaceflight mission to China's Tiangong space station, at Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center | Photo Credit: Reuters
Zhu Yangzhu from the Shenzhou-23 ⁠crew will be staying in space for a year-long mission, authorities said.

The launch ‌comes amid an accelerating race to the moon with the United States, which alleges that Beijing plans to colonise and mine lunar territory and resources — claims Beijing has strongly rejected.

Shenzhou-24, launching ‌aboard a Long March-2F rocket from the Jiuquan ​Satellite Launch Center, is the 41st flight mission of China’s crewed space ⁠program and will complete an in-orbit rotation with ⁠the Shenzhou-23 crew, authorities said.
In orbit, the crew will ‌carry out space science experiments alongside planned station research.

articles.title: Why U.S. President Donald Trump believed he needed to get Jensen Huang back at Nvidia
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump has intervened to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO of Nvidia, following his recent ouster
U.S. President Donald Trump saw little choice but to fight to reinstate Jensen Huang at AI behemoth Nvidia .

The president has staked the nation's economic growth on artificial intelligence, and worried Mr. Huang's ouster was not only tanking the stock market — but also risked putting the U.S. behind Beijing in the race for dominance in the field if Mr. Huang, widely seen by backers and critics as a generational talent in artificial intelligence, were to be poached by a Chinese firm.

And the president, a thrice-married man and real estate maven who has seen his own marital infidelity scrutinised in the press, bristled at Mr. Huang being ousted from the company he built because of extramarital affairs, including one with an executive at a Singapore-based company who U.S. officials suspect was a Chinese spy.

So Mr. Trump engaged in an extraordinary level of behind-the-scenes maneuvering to reinstate Mr. Huang, starting almost immediately after the CEO's fall from grace when he resigned on November 12 as reports trickled out about a trio of affairs.

The U.S. president stated plainly in a CNBC interview on Monday he used his considerable sway to get Mr. Huang his job back. “I spoke to them,” Trump said of the company's board of directors. “Let me just put it that way. And I convinced them.”

Monday's reinstatement was a remarkable turnaround by Nvidia's board, which had insisted days after Mr. Huang’s ouster that it was not considering such a move, even as Trump pushed for it and thousands signed an online petition calling for Huang’s return.

Trump stayed loyal to the iconic CEO who was a trusted adviser to the White House on artificial intelligence and a big donor to the president's ballroom project, arguing the company and America would be best served with Mr. Huang in charge of Nvidia.

Trump is also a big personal believer, and investor, in Nvidia, a leader in the global artificial intelligence industry's boom. At the end of 2025, he had Nvidia holdings worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, according to his annual financial disclosure report filed in June 2026. That's up from the $615,000 to $1.3 million in Nvidia stock in his disclosed holdings at the end of 2024.

The White House has said the president's portfolio is independently managed by third-party financial institutions. “All holdings are maintained in discretionary accounts and invested through computer-based model portfolios that automatically replicate recognized indexes,” said Davis Ingle, a White House spokesman. “Neither President Trump nor any member of his family has any ability to direct, influence, or provide input regarding how the portfolio is invested or when investments are bought or sold.”

Mr. Trump said that the walloping AI stocks had taken following Mr. Huang's sacking helped him make his case. Some of his closest advisers helped persuade the board: Vice President JD Vance, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who as recently as last week had called for a “dramatic shake-up” at Nvidia.

articles.title: 5.6 magnitude earthquake strikes Nepal’s Koshi province close to China border

A magnitude 5.6 earthquake struck eastern Nepal’s Koshi province close to the China border on Tuesday. There were no immediate reports of any damage caused by the tremor.
The earthquake occurred at 7.17 a.m. with its epicentre at Olangchung Gola in Taplejung district, about 275 km east of Kathmandu, according to the National Earthquake Monitoring and Research Centre.

Tremors were also felt by people living in several districts of eastern Nepal.

articles.title: India and Israel: Cut from different cloths
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: In the summer of 2024, I was in Jerusalem. While talking to a senior Israeli diplomat at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the western part of the city, which has been Israel’s seat of power since the 1948-49 war, I asked him about Israel’s relationship with India. India and Israel had built a very close strategic partnership over the past couple of decades. At the same time, India continued to maintain its institutional support for the Palestine cause. I referred to India’s votes at the UN supporting Palestinian national self-determination. India also backed resolutions that condemned Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank and the Israeli occupation of Syria’s Golan Heights. The diplomat said, “India is doing what it has to do, but those positions will not have any impact on the Israeli-India ties.” He also said the partnership had evolved and progressed over the years and under different governments. “There is a consensus in Delhi and there is a consensus in Jerusalem on how we should move forward.”
See my colleague Shobhana K. Nair’s analysis: Rahul Gandhi’s Gaza remarks expose old fault lines between Congress and Left

Others said there is nothing wrong in what Mr. Gandhi said given the close relationship between the two countries. Israel faces increasing international isolation today over its militarism and violence. In the U.S., Israel’s biggest supporter, the political tide is turning against the Jewish nation , as was evident during the midterm elections. But in India, as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu himself pointed out recently, Israel has a lot of supporters. And Mr. Gandhi’s comment reflects the consensus in the Indian political elite across the ideological divide that the relationship with Israel is very significant. Daniel Carmon, a former Israeli ambassador in India, wrote in social media after Mr. Gandhi’s comment that he had several “in-depth meetings” with Mr. Gandhi in the past at the latter’s residence. “The more meetings we had, the clearer his understanding became of the Israeli position and the importance of bilateral relations,” he wrote about Mr. Gandhi.

To be sure, Israel is an important defence partner. While bilateral trade between the two countries stands at an inconsequential $3.7 billion, Israel accounts for roughly 15% of India’s defence imports, making it the third-largest supplier between 2021 and 2025, after Russia (40%) and France (29%). This shift did not begin with Narendra Modi becoming Prime Minister. It was the Congress government under P.V. Narasimha Rao that established full diplomatic relations with Israel in 1992. India also wants to reduce its reliance on Russia. Being excessively dependent on a single country for critical defence supplies is not healthy, and Israel is stepping in to fill this gap. Ideally, a country of India’s size and economic strength should have its own defence industrial base capable of meeting its requirements and supporting its expansion. But India is still some distance from achieving that goal and will continue to depend on imports in the foreseeable future. Israel supplies a range of critical military equipment, including air-defence systems, drones, radars, surveillance networks and precision-guided munitions. India, in turn, is Israel’s largest defence export market by volume, giving New Delhi some leverage in the partnership.

But the picture is incomplete if one looks at just the defence numbers. Israel’s unchecked militarism in its neighbourhood--India’s extended neighbourhood--is a source of regional instability that threatens India’s long-term economic interests. India wants to see a political settlement to the Palestine question. On the other side, most of Israel’s top leadership, across the political spectrum, is united in their opposition to the creation of a Palestine state. Israel’s violence against Palestinians has also deepened its international isolation, making it increasingly unpopular across the Global South. As a country that seeks to represent the voice of the Global South in a multipolar world, India cannot entirely ignore these sentiments.

The Iran war is another example of the divisions between the two countries. The war, launched by Israel and the U.S. against a friendly country in India’s neighbourhood, and the subsequent energy shock posed direct challenges to India’s energy security. At home, Indians are paying more for fuel since the war began and inflation remains high. If hostilities break out again–Israel wants to resume strikes on Iran–there would be another economic blow. At least 23 Indians have been killed in the crossfire in the Persian Gulf region since the war began. The long-term impact of the war on GCC economies will have a direct bearing on the millions of Indians living in the region.

India’s relationship with Israel has evolved over the years, accompanied by shifts in its Palestine policy. I wrote in March 2024 about the changes and continuity in India’s Palestine policy . But any discussion of India’s relationship with Israel would be incomplete without taking into account India’s larger interests in West Asia and the destabilising consequences of Israel’s militarism, even if one sets aside the obvious moral question.

articles.title: Delhi’s rural outskirts are more polluted than the megacity — and crop burning is not the culprit
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: This counter-intuitive phenomenon is driven by the high use of wood, dung and other household fuels for cooking and heating, a study finds.

Days after Diwali earlier this month, Delhi was cloaked in an all-too familiar haze that did not just obscure vision but contained extreme levels of PM2.5, a fine toxic particulate matter that clings to our lungs. But on November 13 the capital broke a record: it was declared the world’s most polluted city .

Delhi’s air quality index, according to Swiss group IQAir, was a “hazardous” 334 on the day, fuelled by vehicular emissions, construction dust and smoke from agricultural burning in its neighbouring villages.

Science, Space & Environment Report: Delhi’s rural outskirts are more polluted than the megacity — and crop burning is not the culprit. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Training vs inference: What’s the distinction at the heart of the Sarvam AI-China models controversy? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Can India build an indigenous AI ecosystem while hosting models developed in China? What is Sarvam’s Token Factory? What does it mean for India’s AI ambitions?

The story so far: Sarvam AI has so far been known for developing its own Artificial Intelligence (AI) models with support from the government’s IndiaAI Mission. On November 16, the Bengaluru-based startup added another part to its business with the launch of Token Factory, a commercial service that gives businesses access to its own models and those developed by other companies, including Chinese firms.

The launch prompted a debate over whether offering Chinese-developed models through a commercial platform aligns with India’s ambition to build indigenous AI capabilities, particularly when a company has received government support.

Hemant Mohapatra, partner at Lightspeed India and an investor in Sarvam, defended the commercial rationale. In a November 18 post on X, he said global AI companies were generating substantial revenue by hosting models, including Chinese ones, on infrastructure in India and serving customers worldwide. He attributed the opportunity to a global shortage of GPUs, which has made computing capacity in India attractive to companies seeking to run their models.

On November 22, Sarvam co-founder Pratyush Kumar issued a clarification on X, addressing questions about the company’s government support, its decision to host foreign-developed models and its commitment to developing its own models. He said Sarvam had used subsidised computing access under the IndiaAI Mission to train its 105B model, while maintaining that its inference business did not conflict with its objective of developing its own models.
Token Factory is an inference platform that allows developers and businesses to access several AI models through a single Application Programming Interface (API).

articles.title: Google denies rumours of large-scale layoffs in India
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: An official Google handle on X noted that “approximately 30 roles were eliminated”
Google has shot down social media rumours about secret, large-scale employee layoffs taking place in India.
An official Google handle on X noted that only around 30 roles were affected and that the rumours of larger layoffs were untrue.

“These rumours are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organisational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a re-prioritisation of work,” posted the company in response to a user on X on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).
The source of this updated information was the Google Cloud India official handle on the X (formerly Twitter) social media platform. The handle had been verified as an official organisation.

The original X user had claimed there were “huge” layoffs at Google India and asked what was happening, while other social media users earlier shared unverified claims about Google employees panicking or being given layoff notices.

Indian tech and IT employees are facing yet another period of instability; this was underscored by Microsoft last month offering voluntary exit packages to around 60,000 staff members, including eligible Indian teams.
The number represented about a quarter of the company’s workforce.
Google has also expanded its voluntary buyout initiative to more countries.

An official Google handle on X noted that “approximately 30 roles were eliminated”

Google has shot down social media rumours about secret, large-scale employee layoffs taking place in India.

An official Google handle on X noted that only around 30 roles were affected and that the rumours of larger layoffs were untrue.

“These rumours are totally inaccurate. Last week, Google Cloud made a small organisational change in India, and approximately 30 roles were eliminated as part of a re-prioritisation of work,” posted the company in response to a user on X on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The source of this updated information was the Google Cloud India official handle on the X (formerly Twitter) social media platform. The handle had been verified as an official organisation.

The original X user had claimed there were “huge” layoffs at Google India and asked what was happening, while other social media users earlier shared unverified claims about Google employees panicking or being given layoff notices.

Indian tech and IT employees are facing yet another period of instability; this was underscored by Microsoft last month offering voluntary exit packages to around 60,000 staff members, including eligible Indian teams.

The number represented about a quarter of the company’s workforce.

fullParagraphs: Three workers died after they entered the septic tank of a gated community in Bachupally on Tuesday (November 24). Inhalation of toxic gases accumulated in the septic tank are suspected as the reason for the deaths.

The community Dinesh Auric, located at APR Enclave in Bachupally, reportedly engaged the services of a firm HR Enviro for periodic cleaning of the septic tank. The three workers sent by the firm arrived at the apartment on Tuesday at 11.30 a.m. to clean the tank. They reportedly entered the tank one after the other, but failed to return.

Receiving information about the incident, forces from the Fire department and Hyderabad Disaster Response & Asset Protection Agency arrived at the location and initiated rescue efforts, but could only retrieve bodies of the workers. The deceased were identified as Pavan Yalla, 20, K. Shanmukha Rao alias Suman, 26, and Suresh, 24, all from Srikakulam district of Andhra Pradesh. Full details about the incident are yet to be received, a press note from HYDRAA informed.

articles.title: 4,324 POCSO cases logged in Karnataka in 2025; police complaints authority member calls for child safety plan in schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Citing 4,324 Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act (POCSO) cases registered in Karnataka in 2025, with nearly 12 cases reported every day, Karnataka State Police Complaints Authority member Mohan Kumar Danappa has urged the School Education Department to introduce a comprehensive 14-point child safety programme across all government, aided and private schools in the State.
Read: Karnataka High Court quashes POCSO case against child’s father, citing abuse of law by mother due to marital discord

In a letter dated November 24 to the Commissioner of the School Education Department, Mr. Danappa called for mandatory POCSO awareness programmes, stronger child protection mechanisms and greater accountability among school managements to prevent sexual offences against children.

articles.title: Student takes grandfather’s revolver to school; classmate shot in accidental firing

fullParagraphs: The incident occurred around 11.30 a.m. when the student from Kodumunda brought a country-made revolver to school and showed it to his classmates

A Class IX student was injured after being shot by a classmate inside a classroom at Parudur Higher Secondary School, Pallippuram, near Thrithala in Palakkad district on Tuesday. The incident occurred around 11.30 a.m. when the student from Kodumunda brought a country-made revolver to school and showed it to his classmates. The gun reportedly went off accidentally during this time, injuring a classmate from Anjumoola.

According to the police, the firearm was discharged twice. The first bullet hit a wall, while the second struck the hand of the classmate. The injured student was taken to a private hospital at Kottakkal near Malappuram, where he is undergoing treatment. Hospital sources said the injury was not serious.

During questioning, the student who brought the gun told the police that it belonged to his grandfather. The revolver had been kept at their house after his grandfather’s death several years ago. The student reportedly took the firearm from home without his mother’s knowledge and brought it to school out of curiosity to show it to his friends. His father, who had worked abroad, died about a month ago.

Police said the revolver was an old weapon. It has been taken into custody and kept as evidence. Deputy Superintendent of Police K.C. Vinu said they launched an investigation into the incident. He said they were also examining the circumstances in which the student accessed the firearm.

Minister for General Education N. Samsudheen has directed the Director of General Education to investigate the incident and submit an urgent report. The police said further action would be taken in accordance with the law.

articles.title: RSP stakes claim to Cabinet-rank equivalent post
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Revolutionary Social Party (RSP), a Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) constituent, on Tuesday (November 24) staked a claim for a Cabinet-level post in the government.
The RSP said it strongly opposed conferring Cabinet status on people outside the Council of Ministers as a means of political rehabilitation.
However, the RSP said the new norm of appointing political figures to Cabinet-rank positions constrained the party from staking its claim for a comparable post for party veteran A.A. Azees.

On Monday, the RSP publicly expressed annoyance at the lack of regular UDF meetings, delays in political appointments to various corporations and boards, and the conferral of Cabinet-rank positions without consultation, and signalled frustration at being bypassed in government.

The RSP had also obliquely telegraphed disaffection with Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan for granting Cabinet-level ranking to Kerala Administrative Commission chairperson and IUML leader M.K. Muneer; Forward Bloc Leader and Keralam government’s special representative in New Delhi, G. Devarajan; and Kerala Congress leader and Chief Whip Apu John Joseph without consultations in the UDF.

The RSP has conveyed its demand in writing to Mr. Satheesan, Congress Working Committee permanent invitee and Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala, Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president and Electricity Minister Sunny Joseph, and United Democratic Front (UDF) convenor, Adoor Prakash.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return.
Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

“Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.
“Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.”
The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23).
The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025.
Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.
The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

fullParagraphs: Shanghai Party Secretary Chen Jining was earlier expected to assume a top leadership role in 2027

A prominent Chinese politician who is a member of the ruling Communist Party of China’s Politburo and was widely tipped for a top national leadership position in 2027 was placed under a shock disciplinary investigation on Tuesday (November 24, 2026).

The surprising announcement of “suspected severe violations” by Chen Jining, who has since 2022 been the top CPC leader in Shanghai and has served on the 25-member Politburo, left political observers in Beijing stunned.

Mr. Chen (62) was tipped to take on a prominent national role in the once-in-five-year Party Congress set for next year, which will see a major reshuffle. President Xi Jinping is expected to begin a fourth term in 2027.

Mr. Chen “is being investigated by the CPC Central Commission for Discipline Inspection and the National Commission of Supervision for suspected severe violations of discipline and laws,” a brief statement said.

Mr. Chen was previously the president of Mr. Xi’s alma mater, Tsinghua University, and served as the mayor of Beijing between 2018 and 2022, before his promotion to the Politburo as the Party Secretary of China’s financial centre, Shanghai.

In Shanghai, Mr. Chen was popular with foreign business representatives and is among the few leaders in the top echelons of the CPC with significant international exposure, having conducted his doctoral studies in environmental engineering at Imperial College London.

Politburo members are rarely investigated, and only half a dozen Politburo-level members in the last three decades have been removed. Notably, removals have often coincided with the run-up to Party Congresses that see leadership promotions and reshuffles.

Another former Shanghai Party Secretary, Chen Liangyu, was removed in 2006, a year before the 2007 Congress that saw the anointment of Mr. Xi as former leader Hu Jintao’s successor. The year of Mr. Xi’s ascension in 2012 saw the removal of Bo Xilai, then Party Secretary in Chongqing.

Under Mr. Xi however, several Politburo-ranked members, including those from the military, have been removed. The former security chief Zhou Yongkang retired from the Politburo Standing Committee, the party’s highest body, in 2012 was placed under investigation in 2014. Another former Chongqing Party Secretary, Sun Zhengcai, was removed in 2017.

Earlier this year, PLA Generals Zhang Youxia and He Weidong were removed, along with former Xinjiang Party Secretary Ma Xingrui. Mr. Chen will be the fourth in the current Politburo to be placed under investigation, a first in China’s recent history.

articles.title: Kaliningrad: Why Russia’s Baltic exclave is a new flashpoint
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Moscow has accused the alliance of increasing military pressure around the strategic exclave and has sent a formal diplomatic note to the NATO over what it sees as attempts to isolate the territory; however, NATO has rejected the accusations, saying its activities in the region are ‘defensive’

On October 1, Russian President Vladimir Putin issued a warning to the West. In a grand hall in Moscow, Mr. Putin sat before an audience of foreign policy experts at the Valdai Discussion Club. “If it comes to a direct attack on the Russian Federation... then, of course, the question of the Russian Federation deploying all types of weapons at our country’s disposal will inevitably and immediately be on the agenda. This is inevitable.”

Mr. Putin continued to insist that Moscow had no plans to attack anyone — neither in 2029, not in 2030, not even in 2050. But if aggression came, he said, Russia would be compelled to respond. European citizens, he added, should understand this clearly. The warning did not appear out of nowhere. For months, NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) countries have been increasing military activities in the Baltic Sea and around Russia’s western borders.

Russia has accused the alliance of increasing military pressure around Kaliningrad and has sent a formal diplomatic note to NATO over what Moscow sees as attempts to isolate the territory. NATO, however, has rejected those accusations, saying its activities in the region are ‘defensive’.

“I can confirm that Russia sent a non-paper to NATO and that we have sent a response, noting that NATO is a defensive alliance and none of our activities or exercises pose a risk to any part of Russia,” said alliance spokesperson Allison Hart. “We strongly denounce the threat of force, including any irresponsible nuclear rhetoric,” she added.

articles.title: Brazil turns heat on Big Tech and Bolsonaro camp over foreign interference in elections
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government

Three weeks after President Lula da Silva’s election victory, Brazilian institutions are tightening the screws on Big Tech over alleged interference in favour of his far-right rival Flávio Bolsonaro during the campaign. The move follows Lula’s pledge to make digital regulation a priority of his government. “This election was one in which we had to overcome interference from outside through digital platforms. We are going to have to regulate them,” Lula told his supporters after winning the election on October 25.

On Saturday (November 14, 2026), the Brazilian government stepped up efforts to pass a bill which would give the country’s competition regulator (CADE) more powers to monitor the Big Tech operations. Pending since September 2025, the bill is modelled on European Union regulations and it faces opposition from Bolsonaro allies.

Meanwhile, both Big Tech and the Bolsonaro camp are feeling the heat. In a landmark ruling on November 10, Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) fined Meta 7.5 million reais (US$1.5 million) for “failing to provide complete information” in a case alleging bias in the distribution of online content. The decision came after a civil society group filed a petition accusing Meta of restricting pro-Lula posts while allowing content favouring Flávio during the campaign. Meta has dismissed the allegations as “false and unfounded”, but internal documents of the company, exposed by Brazilian media, showed that Lula’s Instagram accounts had been restricted during the campaign.

In another decision that can have far-reaching consequences for Flavio and his Liberal Party (PL), a Brazilian Supreme Court judge has ordered the Federal Police (PF) to investigate possible foreign interference in the electoral process, with focus on hidden financing of campaigns. In his order, Justice Flávio Dino cited allegations that two Brazilian businessmen acted on behalf of the US-based Rockbridge Network to raise funds for Flávio’s campaign in the United States. “The prohibition on foreign financing under Brazilian law has a parallel in the US as well. For this reason, it is even more important that resources allegedly originating from that country should not be allowed to influence the Brazilian election,” the judge said in his order.

The Rockbridge Network is an American right-wing organisation co-founded in 2019 by US Vice-President JD Vance and businessman Chris Buskirk, with tech billionaire Peter Thiel bringing them together. Justice Dino has directed the police to investigate whether money and services were channelled to Flávio’s campaign. He also cited concerns over Meta’s handling of political content, including an October 22 report by the company’s Oversight Board highlighting gaps in safeguards for electoral integrity and concerns raised by United Nations observers on October 21.

articles.title: After Donald Trump’s midterm poll rout, South America breathes easy as far-right feels the heat
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Just a day after a blue wave swept across the U.S. in midterms election shaking President Donald Trump’s administration, the fall of Santiago Pena carries significance beyond the borders of the country of seven million people

On Wednesday (November 4, 2026), rising tensions in Asuncion, the capital of Paraguay, turned violent as hundreds of thousands stormed the streets to protest locking out of their accounts in the country’s biggest bank. As fires burned and people anxiously queued outside the collapsed bank, President Santiago Pena, a former shareholder in the bank, announced his resignation.

But as Congress moved to impeach him, Mr. Pena disappeared amid rumours that he had fled to Argentina — just as Brazilian far-right leader Flávio Bolsonaro did last week before fleeing to U.S. after losing the election to President Lula da Silva. “We have information that he left the country without telling anyone. I think he went to Argentina and sought asylum,” said Paraguayan Senator Antonio Velázquez on Thursday (November 5, 2026).

articles.title: Lula da Silva | The Pele of Brazil’s politics
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The left-wing leader’s victory in Brazil, after finishing second in the first round, reflects the deep roots of the Workers’ Party, which built its support base through resistance to the military dictatorship in the early 1980s, as well as the declining appeal of Bolsonarismo

With a smirk, Flávio Bolsonaro squinted at the camera and called President Lula da Silva “nine fingers” in the televised debate just two days before Brazil went to the polls for the presidential runoff. It was a cynical attempt to weaponise an old scar – and a gossip – against the Workers Party’s leader. Lula reacted sharply, reminding the audience how he had lost a finger on his left hand while working in a factory. “If there is anyone who lost a finger at the age of 17, it was me, working at night because I had to work,” Lula said, staring into the cameras. A red-faced Flavio didn’t know where to look. On October 25, Lula made history by becoming the first Brazilian president to finish second in the first round of an election, held on October 4, and go on to win the presidency in the run-off.

Ever since Lula entered politics more than three decades ago, his opponents have peddled the rumour that he deliberately chopped off his own finger to gain sympathy and claim compensation. But those familiar with his life know the struggles that shaped him. Born on October 27, 1945, in a dusty corner of Brazil, Lula grew up amid hunger and deprivation in the state of Pernambuco.

His family migrated to São Paulo in search of a better life, joining thousands who fled the region trapped in poverty and hopelessness. Raised by his mother, Dona Lindu, whose resilience left a lasting impression on him, Lula received only primary education before joining the workforce as a teenager. His mother passed away at 64 in 1980, while Lula was in prison during a workers’ strike. “I believe in a more just country because one day my mother taught me that, even in a simple home, no one can give up,” Lula said on Mother’s Day this year, fighting back tears as he remembered Dona Lindu.

Lula’s journey – from a parched corner of Brazil to the industrial belt of Sao Paulo – was brought to life in Lula, the Son of Brazil , a 2010 film directed by Fábio Barreto. Tracking his life, the film showed how Lula’s political training began on the factory floors of Sao Paulo’s industrial region known for its massive factories.

Amid the clutter of machines and the daily struggle with poverty, Lula rose from an apprentice to a metalworker and trade union leader and became the voice of workers who were not willing to accept low wages and political exclusion. “During the late 1970s, as Brazil’s military dictatorship sought to contain dissent, Lula emerged as one of the most prominent figures in the labour movement. His leadership brought him into direct confrontation with the regime and in 1980 he was arrested for his role in the strikes,” said Mr. Barreto.

articles.title: What do lemurs and opera singers share?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began?

With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him.

Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities.

While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto!
One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery.

Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs.
The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

“The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment 📅 24 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 4 Min Read

📰 What do lemurs and opera singers share?

🎯 Exam Relevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action

Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began?

With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him.

Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities.

While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto!

One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery.

Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs.

The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

“The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

articles.title: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO: 6 CEOs who reclaimed their top positions
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang had resigned due to an alleged Chinese spy scandal on November 12, 2026.

Jensen Huang, co-founder of Nvidia, who had stepped down as the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of the chipmaker, was re-instated in the top job on November 23, 2026. Mr Huang had resigned due to an alleged Chinese spy scandal on November 12, and CFO Colette Kress was appointed as interim CEO.

The board voted unanimously to bring Mr Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, Nvidia said in a statement.
Huang’s return has put the spotlight on the ouster and return of other top bosses. Here’s a look at some of the major names.
Former Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey | Photo Credit: Sandeep Saxena

The return of Mr Jensen Huang at the helm of Nvidia is unique, as reports suggest that senior U.S. government officials left the company’s board confident that he posed no national security risk amid concerns of China vying for the company’s advanced chips. U.S. President Donald Trump also welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.” I believe my ​intervention was very important to get Jensen Huang back,” Mr Trump told CNBC after Mr Huang’s reinstatement, marking an unprecedented intervention by U.S. government officials into the matters of a publicly traded company.

articles.title: Webinar on autoimmune conditions to be held on November 28
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The webinar will examine how autoimmune conditions develop, their common symptoms, the challenges in diagnosis, and current approaches to treatment and long-term management
The Hindu will conduct a free health webinar on Saturday, November 28, 2026, on the topic ‘Understanding Autoimmune Conditions’. The webinar will be held from 11.30 a.m. to 12.30 p.m.

Autoimmune conditions occur when the immune system mistakenly attacks the body’s own tissues and organs. These disorders can affect different parts of the body, including the joints, skin, nervous system and other organs, and may present with a wide range of symptoms.

The session will explore how autoimmune conditions develop, the role of the immune system, and the common signs and symptoms associated with these disorders. It will also discuss early warning signs, including persistent fatigue, joint pain, muscle weakness and neurological symptoms, and explain when these warrant medical attention.

The discussion will examine the challenges involved in diagnosing autoimmune conditions, the role of clinical evaluation and diagnostic tests, and the treatment options available. The panellists will also discuss long-term disease management, monitoring, and the importance of timely diagnosis and appropriate treatment.

Expert panellists include Aishwarya G., Consultant Rheumatologist and Clinical Immunologist, Apollo Speciality Hospitals, Chennai. She will discuss the immune mechanisms underlying autoimmune conditions, common rheumatological disorders, their symptoms, diagnostic approaches and current treatment options.

The panel will also feature Prabash Prabhakaran, Director and Senior Consultant – Neurology, SIMS Hospital, Vadapalani, Chennai. He will discuss autoimmune conditions affecting the nervous system, the neurological symptoms they can cause, approaches to diagnosis and treatment, and the importance of recognising neurological manifestations.
The session will be moderated by Zubeda Hamid, Senior Assistant Editor, The Hindu .
To register, click here or scan the QR code given below.

articles.title: De-notification of MSMER-2023 removes overlapping procedures, but will it safeguard standards of medical education?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Under MSMER-2023, there was a defined escalation path; now, action depends on MARB assessments being initiated, completed and acted upon within a reasonable timeframe

The National Medical Commission (NMC) has de-notified and withdrawn the Maintenance of Standards of Medical Education Regulations, 2023 (MSMER-2023) where medical colleges were liable to face penalty fines for violations of educational standards and infrastructure requirements at medical colleges.

Earlier reports in The Hindu stated NMC’s withdrawal of MSMER-2023 weakens accountability in medical education by removing provisions to fine individual faculty members and administrators up to ₹5 lakh for submitting false information. Although the Medical Assessment and Rating Board (MARB) can still penalise institutions up to ₹1 crore under separate regulations, institutional penalties may be less effective in deterring individual misconduct. Misleading faculty declarations, inflated patient records, or inadequate clinical training going undetected could ultimately put patients at risk.

The NMC justified the withdrawal by arguing that MSMER created overlapping assessment powers with MARB. However, scrapping the regulations entirely raises questions about the necessity of this move, particularly when non-compliance remains common and transparency in medical education is inadequate. Moreover, conflicting appeal deadlines under MARB regulations and the NMC Act could lead to legal disputes and delay enforcement. Ultimately, the NMC must clarify whether the existing regulatory mechanisms are being effectively enforced and whether their outcomes are publicly accessible without which the withdrawal of MSMER risks appearing to be a relaxation of regulatory oversight rather than a simplification of rules.

Medical experts have further warned that deterrence against practices such as ghost faculty and fabricated patient records would potentially expose students and institutions to greater malpractice and mismanagement. While some experts support the removal of regulatory duplication, they emphasise that effective oversight depends on rigorous verification, transparent reporting, consistent penalties and time-bound enforcement. The NMC must therefore demonstrate that MARB can enforce standards as effectively as the withdrawn framework; otherwise, regulatory rationalisation risks becoming a dilution of accountability.

The NMC has clarified that the MSMER introduced a parallel mechanism through which the undergraduate and postgraduate boards could assess institutions, thereby encroaching on the MARB’s mandate. While talking to The Hindu , NMC officials said the denotification is aimed at simplifying regulatory procedures and eliminating overlapping responsibilities, without compromising the quality of medical education.

articles.title: GTA VI is here, and India has taken the day off
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Grand Theft Auto VI is a homecoming, and this time a good part of the city was built in Bengaluru

This week, Grand Theft Auto VI landed on Blinkit, in a collectible box available in select areas across 11 cities. There is no disc inside, only a download code, because Rockstar is selling the game purely as a download, even in stores. That makes for instant gratification of a new kind: the most anticipated game in years can now reach your doorstep in minutes, about as quickly as a loaf of bread, with the code ready to redeem the moment it arrives. Blinkit co-founder Albinder Dhindsa announced the offering on X on November 18, noting that it had taken 13 years for the game to arrive. articles.title: Para-sports selection trials held in Visakhapatnam
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: The District Sports Authority, Visakhapatnam, conducted district-level selection trials in six para-sports disciplines for boys and girls with disabilities aged above 13 years as on November 23 and 24, with 56 athletes participating.

The trials were organised under the aegis of the Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh (SAAP), in association with the Department for Welfare of differently-abled, transgender persons and senior citizens and the Para Sports Association, Visakhapatnam. The initiative was organised in connection with the International Day of Persons with Disabilities, observed every year on December 3.

The disciplines included para athletics, para badminton, para table tennis, para taekwondo, wheelchair fencing and blind goalball. The events were held at the DSA Indoor Stadium, Gopalapatnam, on November 23 and at the SAAP Integrated Sports Complex, Kommadi, on November 24.
Athletes selected at the district level will take part in the State-level competitions scheduled to be held in Vizianagaram district on December 1 and 2.

June Gallyot, District Sports Development Officer (DSDO), Sports Authority of Andhra Pradesh, K. Kavitha, Assistant Director, Department for Welfare of Differently Abled, Sheetal Madan, honorary president of the Para Sports Association, Visakhapatnam and technical official P. Siva Kumar and the Samagra Shiksha coordinator were present.

articles.title: Infant denied birth certificate in West Bengal after father’s name deleted in SIR
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: There have been several instances in Bengal in the last few months in which the residents were denied basic facilities or access to a government scheme after their names were deleted in the SIR

A two-and-a-half-month-old infant in West Bengal ’s Cooch Behar has been denied a birth certificate after her father’s name was found deleted from the electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR ) exercise.

On September 9, Amina Khatun, a resident of Cooch Behar’s Khatamari village, delivered a baby girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital. Following the birth, Ms. Khatun and her husband, Abdul Habib, approached the hospital and the concerned Panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. However, they were reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the Panchayat Pradhan or MLA.
Abdul Habib, the father of the infant. Photo: Special arrangement.

When Mr. Habib approached the MLA of the Dinhata constituency, Ajoy Roy, for such verification, the MLA’s office refused the request. Mr. Habib was told that the certificate could not be issued because his name had been deleted from the electoral roll during the SIR process.

“An official from the MLA office said that I am a Bangladeshi national and therefore I would need to get myself first registered through the National Register of Citizens. Why would I do that? I have been living in India since my birth. My house in Khatamari was built by my grandfather. I have shown them all the documents, but they still refused,” said Mr. Habib. A similar request was also refused by the Block Development Officer (BDO) of Sahebganj on the same grounds, he said.

Mr. Habib is not the only one in his family whose name was deleted during the SIR. Three of his sisters’ names were also deleted. The Election Commission of India (ECI) called them for a hearing, citing a ‘logical discrepancy’ that six other persons also claimed his father as their own.

However, the names of Mr. Habib’s parents, wife Ms. Khatun, and elder sister were included in the voter’s list. He has now appealed before a tribunal to include his name in the voter’s list but the application is awaiting a decision.

The Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR) has strongly objected to the alleged administrative obstruction to issuing the infant’s birth certificate. “Birth registration is a statutory obligation, and every child has the right to immediate registration and legal identity under Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). The child’s right to legal identity must not be linked to the electoral status of her parents. An administrative dispute concerning SIR cannot become a barrier to a newborn child’s fundamental rights,” said the APCR in an official statement, demanding that the government immediately provide her with a birth certificate.

There have been several instances in Bengal in the last few months in which residents were denied basic facilities or access to a government scheme after their names were deleted in the SIR. The SIR held before the Assembly polls in West Bengal saw the removal of 91 lakh names from the electoral rolls of the State.

Earlier in June, Umme Salma, a resident of Cooch Behar district, had to approach the Calcutta High Court after a local fair price shop dealer told her that her entitlement was likely to be discontinued unless she could show proof of an appeal concerning her electoral status after her name was deleted under SIR. The court had directed that the West Bengal government should not take any coercive steps against the petitioner with regard to her monthly ration entitlement without its permission.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity 📅 24 Nov 2026 ⏱️ 5 Min Read

📰 Infant denied birth certificate in West Bengal after father’s name deleted in SIR

🎯 Exam Relevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes

There have been several instances in Bengal in the last few months in which the residents were denied basic facilities or access to a government scheme after their names were deleted in the SIR

A two-and-a-half-month-old infant in West Bengal ’s Cooch Behar has been denied a birth certificate after her father’s name was found deleted from the electoral rolls during the special intensive revision (SIR ) exercise.

On September 9, Amina Khatun, a resident of Cooch Behar’s Khatamari village, delivered a baby girl at Dinhata Sub-Divisional Hospital. Following the birth, Ms. Khatun and her husband, Abdul Habib, approached the hospital and the concerned Panchayat office to obtain their daughter’s birth certificate. However, they were reportedly asked to arrange residential verification from the Panchayat Pradhan or MLA.

Abdul Habib, the father of the infant. Photo: Special arrangement.

When Mr. Habib approached the MLA of the Dinhata constituency, Ajoy Roy, for such verification, the MLA’s office refused the request. Mr. Habib was told that the certificate could not be issued because his name had been deleted from the electoral roll during the SIR process.

“An official from the MLA office said that I am a Bangladeshi national and therefore I would need to get myself first registered through the National Register of Citizens. Why would I do that? I have been living in India since my birth. My house in Khatamari was built by my grandfather. I have shown them all the documents, but they still refused,” said Mr. Habib. A similar request was also refused by the Block Development Officer (BDO) of Sahebganj on the same grounds, he said.

Mr. Habib is not the only one in his family whose name was deleted during the SIR. Three of his sisters’ names were also deleted. The Election Commission of India (ECI) called them for a hearing, citing a ‘logical discrepancy’ that six other persons also claimed his father as their own.

However, the names of Mr. Habib’s parents, wife Ms. Khatun, and elder sister were included in the voter’s list. He has now appealed before a tribunal to include his name in the voter’s list but the application is awaiting a decision.

The Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR) has strongly objected to the alleged administrative obstruction to issuing the infant’s birth certificate. “Birth registration is a statutory obligation, and every child has the right to immediate registration and legal identity under Article 7 of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). The child’s right to legal identity must not be linked to the electoral status of her parents. An administrative dispute concerning SIR cannot become a barrier to a newborn child’s fundamental rights,” said the APCR in an official statement, demanding that the government immediately provide her with a birth certificate.

There have been several instances in Bengal in the last few months in which residents were denied basic facilities or access to a government scheme after their names were deleted in the SIR. The SIR held before the Assembly polls in West Bengal saw the removal of 91 lakh names from the electoral rolls of the State.

Earlier in June, Umme Salma, a resident of Cooch Behar district, had to approach the Calcutta High Court after a local fair price shop dealer told her that her entitlement was likely to be discontinued unless she could show proof of an appeal concerning her electoral status after her name was deleted under SIR. The court had directed that the West Bengal government should not take any coercive steps against the petitioner with regard to her monthly ration entitlement without its permission.
