articles.title: Israel’s Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Gadi Eisenkot called the attacks ‘Jewish terrorism’, saying that ‘extremist groups that set ⁠fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and foreign relations’

Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank ‌early on Sunday (November 22, 2026), starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an ​accusation of “Jewish terrorism” from the man trying to form an Israeli government.

The attacks come nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his ‌majority. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been asked to form a government, though his prospects seem little better.

Reuters saw burned-out Palestinian vehicles and walls spray-painted with slogans ‌such as “Revenge” and “Death to Arabs” in villages near Ramallah. No one immediately claimed responsibility and ‌no ⁠injuries were reported.

Mr. Eisenkot called the attacks “Jewish terrorism”, saying that “extremist groups that set ⁠fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and foreign relations”.

He said the policies of Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, ultra-nationalist ministers in Mr. Netanyahu’s cabinet, had “brought the ​area to the brink of anarchy, ‌and the authorities have yet to address the crisis”.

Mr. Netanyahu has not yet commented, but Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attacks by a “handful of extremists” and said they are “against our values and do not represent the law-abiding citizens of Judea and Samaria” — the biblical ‌names for the West Bank.
“Israeli authorities are firmly committed to enforcing the law against extremist ​violence,” he told the ELNET Jerusalem Summit.
UN bodies and most countries of the world deny the legality of the settlements, which make the ⁠prospect of an independent Palestinian state ever more remote, a position Israel disputes.

Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, while the military condemned the violence, saying soldiers and police ‌had been dispatched to the areas of Deir as-Sudan, Deir Abu Masha’al, Kafr Malik and At-Tuwani “following reports and footage showing vehicles being set on fire and graffiti being sprayed in the area”.

Mr. Ben-Gvir replied in an X post that Mr. Eisenkot’s condemnation amounted to selling out to Arab parties, which could become part of a possible new government. Mr. Smotrich favours settlement expansion and wants Israel to annex the West Bank.

Gadi Eisenkot called the attacks ‘Jewish terrorism’, saying that ‘extremist groups that set ⁠fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and foreign relations’

Israeli militant settlers attacked Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank ‌early on Sunday (November 22, 2026), starting fires and scrawling racist graffiti, residents said, prompting an ​accusation of “Jewish terrorism” from the man trying to form an Israeli government.

The attacks come nearly a month after an inconclusive election stripped incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of his ‌majority. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has been asked to form a government, though his prospects seem little better.

Reuters saw burned-out Palestinian vehicles and walls spray-painted with slogans ‌such as “Revenge” and “Death to Arabs” in villages near Ramallah. No one immediately claimed responsibility and ‌no ⁠injuries were reported.

Mr. Eisenkot called the attacks “Jewish terrorism”, saying that “extremist groups that set ⁠fire to vehicles and homes are undermining regional stability, putting lives at risk and doing grave damage to Israel’s national security and foreign relations”.

He said the policies of Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, ultra-nationalist ministers in Mr. Netanyahu’s cabinet, had “brought the ​area to the brink of anarchy, ‌and the authorities have yet to address the crisis”.

Mr. Netanyahu has not yet commented, but Foreign Minister Gideon Saar condemned the attacks by a “handful of extremists” and said they are “against our values and do not represent the law-abiding citizens of Judea and Samaria” — the biblical ‌names for the West Bank.

“Israeli authorities are firmly committed to enforcing the law against extremist ​violence,” he told the ELNET Jerusalem Summit.

UN bodies and most countries of the world deny the legality of the settlements, which make the ⁠prospect of an independent Palestinian state ever more remote, a position Israel disputes.

Israeli police said they opened an investigation into the attacks, while the military condemned the violence, saying soldiers and police ‌had been dispatched to the areas of Deir as-Sudan, Deir Abu Masha’al, Kafr Malik and At-Tuwani “following reports and footage showing vehicles being set on fire and graffiti being sprayed in the area”.

articles.title: Japan-Europe spacecraft BepiColombo begins orbit of Mercury, with a glitch reported
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface

After an eight-year journey, the European-Japanese spacecraft BepiColombo has begun orbiting the solar system's smallest ​and innermost planet Mercury, though the European Space Agency said ‌on Sunday (November 22, 2026) a glitch has occurred involving its thrusters.

Mercury, ​only slightly larger than Earth's moon, ⁠is the least explored of the four planets in the inner solar system, with BepiColombo only the third spacecraft to visit the ‌planet and just the second to orbit it.
It is a joint mission of the European Space ‌Agency, or ESA, and the Japan Aerospace Exploration ‌Agency, ⁠or JAXA.

ESA confirmed on Saturday (November 21) that BepiColombo ⁠had begun its orbit. In a social media post on Sunday (November 22), ESA said the spacecraft had a successful entry into orbit, but during the ​manoeuver, "the thruster burn was shorter ‌than planned following a software issue."
"The spacecraft is safe and teams at ESOC (the European Space Operations Centre) are working to understand what happened," ESA said, adding that "updates will ‌be provided on Monday."

The robotic spacecraft, launched in ​2018, is a composite of ESA's Mercury Planetary Orbiter and JAXA's Mercury Magnetospheric Orbiter, which have different ⁠scientific objectives and are due to separate on December 9 and 10. Routine science operations are slated to commence ‌in April.

The mission will seek to answer questions about Mercury such as why it has a magnetic field, why ice exists in the polar craters of a sun-scorched planet, and what is the nature of enigmatic depressions called "hollows" on its surface.
Mercury's surface looks similar to that ‌of the Moon, with numerous impact craters. There are expanses of ​smooth terrain as well as cliffs, some up to a mile (1.6 km) tall.

Mercury is about 60% ⁠closer to the Sun than Earth. That means that from ⁠its surface, the Sun appears more than three times as large and seven times as luminous ‌as it does when seen from Earth. Mercury's diameter of 3,032 miles (4,880 km) is less than 40% of ​Earth's diameter of 7,926 miles (12,753 km).

articles.title: Anthropic IPO: Tracing an ‘unusual’ AI company’s race to the top
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Set up as a Public Benefit Corporation, Anthropic warns that AI could be dangerous, yet races to build the most powerful models. Charts and a timeline unpack the journey and contradictions of the AI company behind the largest-ever IPO

Minutes before Anthropic, the maker of Claude, began trading on Nasdaq on November 19, its co-founder and president Daniela Amodei opened her short speech by calling it an “unusual” company, one many even call “weird”.

Founded in May 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees who left over what they saw as a culture that did not put AI safety and alignment first, Anthropic is registered as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), a structure that legally binds the company to weigh public benefit alongside profit.

Its CEO Dario Amodei has consistently warned about the existential risks of misaligned AI models and pushed for regulation and a slowdown in the race to build frontier models. Rivals and some critics, however, have called this posturing. The provocatively titled “MisAnthropic Statement”, released on the eve of the IPO and signed by a few prominent figures from different fields, said Anthropic was not a safe AI company and urged rejection of its “reckless attempt to amass power in the name of the greater good”.
The charts and timeline below trace the unconventional journey of a company seen as a harbinger of everything unusual unfolding in the AI zeitgeist.

Anthropic raised $81.3 billion despite listing during a market slump — with many beginning to wonder whether the ballooning investments in AI were a bubble — and against the backdrop of the Republican rout in the U.S. midterms and the Nvidia scandal. It broke the record for the largest-ever IPO, set by Elon Musk’s SpaceX just five months earlier in a more bullish market.

Set up as a Public Benefit Corporation, Anthropic warns that AI could be dangerous, yet races to build the most powerful models. Charts and a timeline unpack the journey and contradictions of the AI company behind the largest-ever IPO

Minutes before Anthropic, the maker of Claude, began trading on Nasdaq on November 19, its co-founder and president Daniela Amodei opened her short speech by calling it an “unusual” company, one many even call “weird”.

Founded in May 2021 by seven former OpenAI employees who left over what they saw as a culture that did not put AI safety and alignment first, Anthropic is registered as a Public Benefit Corporation (PBC), a structure that legally binds the company to weigh public benefit alongside profit.

Its CEO Dario Amodei has consistently warned about the existential risks of misaligned AI models and pushed for regulation and a slowdown in the race to build frontier models. Rivals and some critics, however, have called this posturing. The provocatively titled “MisAnthropic Statement”, released on the eve of the IPO and signed by a few prominent figures from different fields, said Anthropic was not a safe AI company and urged rejection of its “reckless attempt to amass power in the name of the greater good”.

The charts and timeline below trace the unconventional journey of a company seen as a harbinger of everything unusual unfolding in the AI zeitgeist.

Anthropic raised $81.3 billion despite listing during a market slump — with many beginning to wonder whether the ballooning investments in AI were a bubble — and against the backdrop of the Republican rout in the U.S. midterms and the Nvidia scandal. It broke the record for the largest-ever IPO, set by Elon Musk’s SpaceX just five months earlier in a more bullish market.

articles.title: Scientists report strong new evidence that specially bred mosquitoes can fend off dengue
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s
Children who lived in Brazilian neighbourhoods buzzing with a special kind of mosquito were far less likely to catch dengue or another worrisome virus, chikungunya, researchers reported Saturday.

The major study of more than 5,700 children in one of the world's dengue hot spots offers new evidence that breeding mosquitoes unable to transmit these viruses can be a viable strategy rather than solely relying on pesticides and trying to avoid getting bitten.

In neighbourhoods populated by these so-called Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes, researchers found about a 69% reduction in dengue and chikungunya infections in schoolchildren compared to similar neighbourhoods — an effect sustained even during Brazil's severe 2024 dengue outbreak, said Dr. Sri Edupuganti of Emory University, part of the international research team.
The researchers reported the findings at a meeting of the American Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene.

“This is really exciting,” said David Hamer, a global health expert at Boston University who wasn't involved with the Brazilian study. He predicts that pairing more use of these Wolbachia mosquitoes with existing steps to fight mosquito-borne disease could “knock dengue down to much lower levels” in many places.
The latest research comes as Florida grapples with an unusually large outbreak of the virus, what appears to be the biggest in any U.S. state since at least the 1940s.

Usually in the continental US, dengue is found mostly in people who travelled internationally. But as of Friday, Florida health officials had tallied more than 650 locally acquired cases, about three-quarters of them in Hillsborough County, home to Tampa.
Outside the U.S., the nonprofit World Mosquito Program has pioneered the Wolbachia strategy.

How it works: Scientists breed mosquitoes to carry a kind of bacteria called Wolbachia. It is harmless to people and common in many insects, although not dengue-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitoes. The bacteria dramatically reduce the mosquitoes' ability to transmit certain viruses. Female mosquitoes spread the bacteria to their offspring, so releasing enough of the specially bred insects — males and females — into an area allows Wolbachia to gradually become established in the local mosquito population.

Field trials and other studies in Indonesia and elsewhere have shown the strategy can significantly lower dengue diagnoses. But because people with mild symptoms may not be diagnosed, the new study in Belo Horizonte, Brazil, went further. Researchers tested blood for signs of dengue, chikungunya or the Zika virus.

articles.title: Yamuna 60% clean, water safe to drink; entire river to be cleaned by 2030: Delhi Minister Sirsa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: “60% of Yamuna jii is totally clean… Clean means so clean that even you can drink that water,” Delhi Minister Sirsa said, urging people to visit the river and see for themselves

Delhi Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Monday (November 23, 2026) said 60% of the Yamuna has been cleaned so much so that its water is now potable, adding that the entire river will be cleaned up by 2029 or 2030.

He was speaking at the launch of Uber’s “One Less Car” report in New Delhi. Mr. Sirsa credited Chief Minister Rekha Gupta and the Union government’s support over the last two years for the cleaning of the river.
He said work began at one end of the river and will move to the other, which is why 60% is done and not the whole stretch.
“60% of Yamuna jii is totally clean… Clean means so clean that even you can drink that water,” he said, urging people to visit the river and see for themselves.

Mr. Sirsa said the city's sewage goes through drains into the Yamuna, and a clean river is impossible unless that sewage is treated. He said the government is using sewage treatment plants (STPs) to deal with the issue.

articles.title: PM Modi holds bilateral talks with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah; trade, investment, connectivity on agenda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah, on a two-day State visit, laid a wreath at Raj Ghat and received a Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan before the talks at Hyderabad House

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Nepali counterpart Balendra Shah arrived at Hyderabad House on Monday (November 23, 2026) to hold bilateral talks, to review India-Nepal relations and explore avenues for strengthening cooperation across key sectors.
The discussions are expected to focus on strengthening economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development.

Both countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering several areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development. Connectivity and energy cooperation are also expected to feature prominently during the visit.

The two sides are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in these sectors and lay foundation stones for upcoming initiatives, reflecting their efforts to expand cross-border cooperation. Beyond government-level engagements, the visit will also feature a Nepal-India Business Forum aimed at attracting Indian investment to Nepal.
The forum will provide a platform for business representatives from both countries to explore opportunities for collaboration and strengthen commercial ties.

Mr. Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of Mr. Shah and his 34-member government delegation. The Nepal Prime Minister is accompanied by Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle, Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal, Chief Advisor to the Prime Minister Kumar Byanjankar and other senior government officials.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Shah paid tribute to Mahatma Gandhi, by laying a wreath at his memorial at Raj Ghat, as part of his State visit to India. He also signed the guestbook at the memorial. Before this, he received a ceremonial Guard of Honour at Rashtrapati Bhavan, with Mr. Modi in attendance.

The two-day State visit is expected to provide an opportunity for both sides to take stock of their bilateral partnership, review ongoing cooperation and explore ways to expand engagement across areas of shared interest.

articles.title: Lights out after defeat: 50 streetlights disappear from village after BJP candidate loses in Rajasthan’s Tonk
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: However, Govardhan Choudhary, assistant engineer with the electricity department in Peeplu, said the streetlights had been installed without authorisation and were removed in accordance with departmental policy

Hours after a BJP candidate lost the Panchayat Samiti elections, around 50 streetlights installed in a village in Rajasthan’s Tonk district were removed by electricity department workers, according to villagers.

However, Govardhan Choudhary, assistant engineer with the electricity department in Peeplu, said the streetlights had been installed without authorisation and were removed in accordance with departmental policy.
The incident took place in Ward 2 of Peeplu Panchayat Samiti, where BJP candidate Priyanka Sharma lost to her Congress rival Dhanna Lal by 751 votes.
Ms. Priyanka is the wife of Alok Sharma, personal assistant to BJP MLA Ram Sahay Verma of Niwai constituency.
According to villagers, the streetlights were installed on October 24 during the election campaign to illuminate streets and residential areas that had remained dark after sunset.
A few hours after the results were declared on Friday (November 20, 2026), electricity department workers arrived in a vehicle and removed the lights.
“The lights were installed in an unauthorised manner,” Mr. Choudhary said, adding that similar action would be taken against unauthorised streetlights in other wards.

Villagers questioned the timing of the action, alleging that the lights were removed because the BJP candidate had lost the election. They said the installations had provided relief from darkness and were appreciated by residents.
MLA Ramsahay Verma denied that he or his personal assistant’s wife had any role in the removal of the lights.
Rajasthan / Bharatiya Janata Party / local elections / Indian National Congress

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit LIVE: Balen Shah begins bilateral visit; energy, connectivity on agenda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: This is Balen Shah's first official bilateral foreign visit since taking office in March. He travelled to the U.S. in September to attend the United Nations General Assembly

Saryu-Kamala Express, which will run between Ayodhya and Janakpur, Nepal, was inaugurated today at the Ayodhya Cantt Railway Station via video conferencing by PM Narendra Modi and Nepal PM Balen Shah.

Nepal PM Balendra Shah after paying homage to Mahatma Gandhi at Raj Ghat today, wrote in the memorial’s visitor book describing truth as “a power unmatched by any force” and calling compassion “the ultimate strength”.

Linking Gandhi’s legacy with Nepal’s heritage, the Nepalese PM added, “On behalf of the people and Government of Nepal, I offer my deepest tribute. Coming from the birthplace of Lord Buddha, I behold in Gandhiji’s legacy that very same immortal light: the profound truth that compassion is the ultimate strength, and that true leadership lies in selfless service to the humblest among us.”

The Ministry of External Affairs said, “India and Nepal share close and friendly relations, rooted in historical, cultural and civilisational links and strong people-to-people ties. Bilateral cooperation has witnessed progress across diverse sectors, including trade and commerce, development partnership, energy and water resources, and physical and digital connectivity, with growing engagement in newer areas such as start-ups, technology and innovation, and sports”.
Prime Minister Modi will also host an official luncheon in honour of his Nepalese counterpart and his 34-member government delegation.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the start of a direct rail service between Ayodhya and Janakpur in Nepal will open a new chapter in the centuries-old spiritual and cultural ties between the two regions and would strengthen India-Nepal relations and facilitate pilgrimage for crores of devotees.

India and Nepal discussions are expected to focus on strengthening economic cooperation, particularly in trade, transportation, investment and infrastructure development. Both countries are also expected to exchange memorandums of understanding (MoUs) covering several areas of mutual interest, including education, health, agriculture, sports, disaster management and human resource development.

Connectivity and energy cooperation are also expected to feature prominently during the visit. The two sides are expected to inaugurate several completed projects in these sectors and lay foundation stones for upcoming initiatives, reflecting their efforts to expand cross-border cooperation.

Former Nepal PM Jhala Nath Khanal said Nepal and India should maintain cordial relations and expand comprehensive cooperation, while expressing concern that Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah had not prepared a common national agenda ahead of his ongoing visit to India.

“There are many expectations. And there are some irritants also in our relations which have to be eliminated. And the relations between our two countries should be comprehensively developed based on five principles of peaceful coexistence and neighbourliness,” Mr. Khanal said.

articles.title: In 12 states, NGO Pratham’s Second Chance Programme is helping women school dropouts appear for their Class X Board exams
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: As a significant percentage of older girls and women in India have not completed secondary education, this 14-year-old initiative focuses on helping them restart their educational journey and direct it towards earning a livelihood

In a tranquil residential enclave at Vijaypura in Devanahalli, 40 kilometres from Bengaluru city, a modest abode has been converted into a classroom, the walls supporting a mixed population of subjects: on one patch of a wall, Kannada vowels and consonants and scientific diagrams enjoy joint tenancy.

Women frantically take down notes as the blackboard gets busy. From time to time, someone would look up from the note-taking to clarify doubts. At this hour, the doubts pertain to monohybrid cross and dihybrid cross. Navyanthi D.N., the science teacher, offers patient answers.

It is a motley class of learners, consisting of Asha workers, a tailor, a young mother with a toddler on her lap watching the phone, noon meal staff working in schools, and determined homemakers in good numbers. An employee with the Kempegowda International Airport makes a dash for the door around noon; she had sought permission to leave the class early to be present at work.

This is one of the many learning clusters run as part of the Pratham-Jameel Second Chance programme, an initiative by the Pratham Education Foundation, to support girls and women who have dropped out of school before completing secondary education. At the Devanahalli Block, this programme is in its second year.

Approximately 24 lakh students fail in Class X every year, and a vast number of them drop out of the formal education system, says a study from the Ministry of Education. Efforts to get them to progress to Class XI through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS) meet with modest success. An analysis report by the Ministry of Education, published in The Hindu in May 2023, states the failure rates range between 47% and 55%.
Given this, interventions by NGOs such as Pratham become significant and essential. Pratham has been bringing out the ASER (Annual Status of Education Report) since 2005.

Started in 2011 as a pilot in Maharashtra, the Second Chance Programme was extended to seven states. Currently, it is being run in 12 states, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Rajasthan, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.

After many door-to-door mobilisation campaigns to enrol women candidates, the new academic year of the Second Chance Programme began in July 2026 in most cities. The foundation course, typically covering lessons taught in the upper middle classes, soaks up three to four months.
Mothers’ groups in neighbourhoods help the ground staff get information about other women or older girls who might be interested in completing class X.

Their ground staff’s tasks include persuading family members to support the women to pursue studies and have a secondary school leaving certificate no matter what the age of the person is. The persuasion sometimes has to be targeted at the women who have to take up the studies.

articles.title: Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif to undertake official visit to Russia
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is set to undertake his first official visit to Russia, followed by a trip to Iran for a regional summit.
The three-day visit to Russia will begin on November 30, aiming to strengthen bilateral ties by securing energy and investment agreements, reported Dawn .

During his meeting with Russian President Vladi­mir Putin, discussions are expected to focus on ene­rgy cooperation, defence, trade, regional security and investment, a source in the Prime Minister’s Office told Dawn.
The revival of Pakistan Steel Mills, established with Russian assistance, is also likely to feature prominently, alongside potential Russian investment in Pakistan’s oil and gas sectors.

The two countries are likely to examine possibilities for Russian cooperation in restoring the industrial facility, alongside broader initiatives aimed at supporting Pakistan’s industrial development.
Later, Prime Minister Shehbaz will be travelling to Iran for the 18th Economic Coo­peration Organisation (ECO) Summit from December 3-4, according to Dawn .
Leaders of 10 member States will discuss regional trade, connectivity, energy, transportation, investment and industrial cooperation.
The summit comes ahead of Pakistan assuming the ECO chairmanship for 2026-27.

articles.title: U.S. panel urges India dialogue for Dalai Lama succession, warns of China legitimacy contest
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest

A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended setting up a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, contending that China may turn the process into an international contest over legitimacy.

A U.S. Congressional panel has recommended establishing a senior-level channel with India for succession contingency planning for the 14th Dalai Lama, arguing that China may turn the process into an international legitimacy contest.

The U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission, in a report to the U.S. Congress, made a strong pitch to recognise the Gaden Phodrang Trust as the sole legitimate authority to identify and recognise the successor to the 14th Dalai Lama.
The report by the bipartisan Commission said China was likely to use coercive tools to shape the outcome of the succession process.
It said that the U.S. Congress should adopt a policy of not recognising any successor to the Dalai Lama who is selected or installed by China.

“To carry out this policy and ensure U.S. government readiness for the Dalai Lama’s succession, Congress should direct the Secretary of State to… establish a senior-level channel with the Government of India for succession contingency planning, including intelligence sharing on Chinese influence operations,” the report said.

It also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to lead an internal interagency tabletop exercise on succession scenarios, with participation by the National Security Advisor, the Director of National Intelligence, and the Secretary of Defence.

The commission also asked the U.S. Secretary of State to conduct Track 1.5 and Track 2 dialogues and tabletop exercises with Indian counterparts on the political and security implications of succession scenarios.
The Commission also wanted the U.S. to coordinate with allies and partners on a diplomatic response that denies international legitimacy to any successor selected by China.

It also wanted the U.S. to counter succession-related influence operations by strengthening the Central Tibetan Administration’s cybersecurity and resilience against China’s cyber and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled disinformation campaigns.

articles.title: Automation system problem at Delta causes flight delays as Americans travel for Thanksgiving
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: The Delta delays come as Americans have been encountering a growing number of problems with technology that are increasingly disrupting their lives

Over 1,000 Delta flights were delayed Sunday (November 22, 2026) after an automated system that calculates an aircraft's weight malfunctioned during a busy time for travel ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

The airline said Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning that its teams were using manual workarounds to get flights off the ground while they sought to restore the automation system that ensures an aircraft isn't too heavy to fly. Hours later, Delta said that system was once again working, though flights were still not back to normal.
The airline said it was helping passengers who needed hotel rooms or meals but hoped to have all the delayed flights in the air by the end of the day.

On Sunday (November 22, 2026) morning, the Federal Aviation Administration issued about an hourlong ground stop to some flights into Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, which is Delta's hub and one of the busiest airports in the world.

Complying with the weight and balance limits of an aircraft is critical to flight safety, according to an FAA document, and going above the limit can compromise the structural integrity of the aircraft.
The agency said on X that the delays weren't related to FAA air traffic systems.

Earlier this month, a malfunction in th e FAA’s network led to the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years . The stop lasted for more than four hours, and carriers canceled and delayed swaths of flights as they worked to recover. Just days after that, United Airlines saw its own system outage — forcing it to delay departing flights.

The Delta delays come as Americans have been encountering a growing number of problems with technology that are increasingly disrupting their lives. And the disruptions came just days before the Thanksgiving holiday, the busiest travel season in the United States.

As of Sunday (November 22, 2026) evening, the flight-tracking website FlightAware said 58%, or about 2,000, of Delta's flights were delayed; it wasn't immediately clear how many of those involved flights into or out of the Atlanta airport.

FlightAware said that about 58% of flights out of the Atlanta airport were delayed while about 50% of flights destined for the airport were delayed. The vast majority of flights at the Atlanta airport are operated by Delta.

articles.title: How long is too long on the throne?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: While there is no single magic number of minutes that is just the right amount of time to sit on the toilet, the broad agreement is up to 5 minutes. Scrolling your phone while sitting for long stretches of time may increase your risk of haemorrhoids

Every time I called my cousin Arun* around 9 a.m., his voice would echo, as though he were in a bathroom. “I’m on the throne, I’ll call you in 20 minutes,” he would say. The first time I heard this, it took me a while to understand what ‘the throne’ was, and as if that was not confusing enough, what was he doing there for 20 minutes. Perplexed, I asked him why he had the phone in the bathroom when he was doing his morning business, to which he casually replied that he would sit on the throne solving Wordle, crosswords and reading the news until he ‘downloaded’. A couple of months ago he told me that he was diagnosed with early stages of haemorrhoids and was on treatment. I advised him on this matter, stressing how his morning ritual could be contributing to his condition. This ultimately led to his ‘conscious reduction of phone time in the bathroom’. His words, not mine. Recently, he proudly announced that his scheduled ‘throne time’ was now down to six minutes, every morning after breakfast.

Bathroom humour is universal. Cinema is no exception — it has found humour and dependable plotlines from this predictable ritual. Just one instance is in Lokesh Kanagaraj’s Vikram , where a character pulling the flush coincides with the house exploding. Thankfully, the consequences of spending 20 minutes on the toilet are far less dramatic.
Science, Space & Environment Report: How long is too long on the throne?. This milestone highlights indigenous research, technological self-reliance, and environmental sustainability.

articles.title: Bisleri says it’s water ‘safe for consumption’ after FSSAI sanctions prosecution, says it has received no notice
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The company said five of six samples collected from its Goa facility in September 2025 met applicable standards, while an independent test found the bromate level in the disputed sample within the prescribed limit

Bisleri International has maintained that its packaged drinking water is safe for consumption, disputing the findings of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), which has sanctioned prosecution against the company after a water sample was declared unsafe following laboratory tests.

In a statement issued on Monday (November 23, 2026), the company said the matter related to a batch manufactured in September 2025 at its Goa facility, one of 143 plants in its network, and dated back about 14 months.

Bisleri said the FSSAI collected six samples from the facility on September 30, 2025, of which five met all applicable standards. The sixth sample recorded a bromate level of 12 micrograms per litre, against the prescribed limit of 10 micrograms per litre.

Following an appeal by the company on November 22, 2025, the FSSAI referred the sample to a referral laboratory for retesting. Bisleri said the referral laboratory found the bromate level to be within the prescribed limit, but separately flagged the presence of polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).

The findings came after the initial laboratory examination had found the sample non-compliant with the prescribed bromate limits, and declared it unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The referral laboratory also declared the sample unsafe, citing the detection of PAHs. Based on the laboratory findings, the FSSAI subsequently sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri.

Questioning the differing test results, Bisleri said the difference between the two sets of findings raised questions that it believed warranted clarification. The company said it arranged for the same sample to be tested independently at an FSSAI-approved laboratory, where the bromate level was also found to be within the prescribed limit.
Bisleri said it submitted the independent test results to the FSSAI’s Western Regional Office along with a formal letter dated February 2, 2026.

“We received no further communication from FSSAI after that submission and understood the matter to be closed. To date, Bisleri has received no notice by email or in hard copy and has been unable to locate the reported notice on FSSAI’s website,” a company spokesperson said.

The company’s management is deciding on the next steps, the spokesperson said. The company said it maintained stringent quality controls, including more than 90 tests across its 10-step manufacturing process. It added that it would continue to cooperate with the FSSAI and address the matter through the appropriate regulatory process.

D eepavali, the festival of lights, left a trail of dark smoke across large parts of India’s northern plains, especially around the national capital, Delhi, where 80 million people, particularly infants and the elderly, are struggling to breathe. The Air Quality Index (AQI) at several locations in the National Capital Region (NCR) had touched 400, indicating the severity of the conditions. Other cities and towns in the north, south, east and west, though better off than the NCR because of favourable weather and geographical advantages, do not have pristine air either. Air in most Indian cities contains pollutants, including particulate matter, at levels about eight times higher than the threshold set by the World Health Organization. The worst part of the problem is its dire predictability, except for concessions from the weather. The costly lessons from the capital have implications for the entire country.

The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) swiftly moved up the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) from Stage I to Stage III within 15 days. The Commission, a statutory body established as an emergency response to toxic air conditions, has been cracking down on farm fires in Punjab, with its teams visiting fields to check incidents of stubble burning. PAVAN-I3C, the CAQM’s new Integrated Command and Control Centre, seeks to capture non-compliance in industries, traffic and transport systems and trigger immediate action against pollution spikes. Construction and demolition (C&D) activities have been halted until the 20th of this month. Inspections of construction sites and checks of Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCC) are also vigorous. Last week, in an unprecedented move, CAQM directed Delhi and other NCR States to plan reduction of annual pollution levels by 15-20% forthwith.

Regulatory moves, however essential, are not enough. Fines and work stoppages offer only partial deterrence, while obstructions and congestion on roads are an outright failure of enforcement. Institutional compliance, enforcement and monitoring by agencies are paramount, but civic behaviour is equally critical.

It would be unimaginable in many other countries for vehicle owners to be reminded of the pollution caused by their vehicles only during the months when the air becomes unbreathable. If clean air is part of the right to life, citizens also have a charter of duties to follow.

People complain and curse, and even silently suffer sickness from foul air, but sensitive and responsive behaviour remains elusive. The expansion of metro services and the availability of more public transport have not persuaded private car owners to switch. The Supreme Court went the extra mile by allowing firecrackers this Deepavali, while imposing justifiable restrictions on their toxic content and duration of use. Yet, citizens’ responses have not remotely matched the severity of the problem. It might seem contradictory, but many would like to reap all the dividends of GRAP without complying with its requirements.

articles.title: What is the HPV vaccine’s role in preventing cervical cancer?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The HPV vaccine is not used to cure cancer; it also does not cure HPV if it is present. What it does, is ensure that some of the most detrimental types of HPV do not enter and infect the body in the first place

When discussing cervical cancer, what often gets left out is that it is one of the most preventable of cancers. Despite this, cervical cancer continues to be a cause of thousands of deaths among women every year, not only in India, but in many parts of the world. In many such cases, the condition is detected far too late, leaving limited room for intervention. The issue therefore, is not a gap in science, but a gap in awareness

The main culprit in cervical cancer is a virus that is very common, human papillomavirus, or HPV for short. HPV primarily spreads through close skin-to-skin contact, most often during sexual intercourse. The virus is so widespread that virtually everyone, both men and women, at some point in their lifetime, will be infected without even realising it. More often than not, the immune system gets rid of the virus without causing any damage.

• The main culprit in cervical cancer is a virus that is very common, human papillomavirus, or HPV for short. HPV primarily spreads through close skin-to-skin contact, most often during sexual intercourse. The virus is so widespread that virtually everyone, both men and women, at some point in their lifetime, will be infected without even realising it. More often than not, the immune system gets rid of the virus without causing any damage.

articles.title: Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of population: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: SAMPADA covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories

According to a survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), severe anaemia was observed in less than 2% of people in the majority of age groups. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025 was released on Monday (November 23, 2026).

It showed that children aged 12-59 months had 42% anaemia prevalence, adolescent girls aged 10-19 years had anaemia prevalence of 46%, adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20–59 years had 22-23% anaemia prevalence, whereas women of reproductive age had 56% prevalence.
The survey also found that mild anaemia constitutes a substantial proportion of the overall anaemia burden.

“SAMPADA provides nationally representative estimates of anaemia across children, adolescents, adults, pregnant and lactating women and older adults, together with detailed information on micronutrient deficiencies to evaluate potential causes of anaemia. It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys. The comprehensive anaemia profiling in the SAMPADA survey provides an evidence base to strengthen the ongoing national efforts towards Anaemia Mukt Bharat,” said Rajiv Bahl, secretary, Department of Health Research.

The report noted that about half of anaemic women, including pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls, and children, have mild anaemia, indicating considerably lower risk of serious health consequences than moderate or severe anaemia. Anaemia prevalence is much lower among adolescent boys, adult and older men, and even among those affected, three-fourths have only mild anaemia, said the release issued by the Union Health Ministry.

SAMPADA represents one of the largest and most comprehensive nutrition surveys undertaken globally. The survey covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin estimation across different age, sex, and physiological groups.

“A major strength of SAMPADA is the use of gold standard method of venous blood sampling and automated analysers for haemoglobin estimation, providing greater accuracy and reproducibility. In a sub-sample, the survey also assessed iron status, folate, vitamin B12, together with inflammatory biomarkers C-reactive protein (CRP) and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) to obtain national level prevalence estimates,” the release said.
Iron deficiency accounts for about half of the anaemia cases in women, adolescent girls, and children, said the report.

The micronutrient assessment showed that although iron deficiency is the predominant contributor to anaemia in vulnerable population groups, it accounts for about half of the overall anaemia burden, highlighting the need to simultaneously address multiple nutritional and non-nutritional causes of anaemia, including infections, hemoglobinopathies, and inflammation related to chronic disease.

However, the prevalence of vitamin B12 and folate deficiency was similar in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals across population groups, indicating a limited contribution of these micronutrient deficiencies to anaemia in India.

articles.title: India’s improved performance in Asia Power Index a reality check for Congress: BJP
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: India improved its score by 0.5, reaching 40.5, which marks the narrowest gap since 2018 between its score and China’s, which stands at 73.6, as per the Lowy Institute metric

The BJP on Monday (November 23, 2026) claimed that the Congress got a reality check with India’s improved standing in the Lowy Institute’s Asia Power Index 2026, hitting out at the Opposition party over its criticism of the country’s economy and asserting that India was consolidating its position as a “major power” in the region.
India improved its score by 0.5, reaching 40.5, which marks the narrowest gap since 2018 between its score and China’s, which stands at 73.6, as per the Lowy Institute metric.

Its report said India has consolidated its position as the third-most powerful country and a “major powerhouse” in Asia, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi rated as the second-most effective regional leader.
According to the Index, the U.S. and China are “superpowers in Asia for 2026”, with the U.S.’ score being the highest, at 78.9.

Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, senior party leader Ravi Shankar Prasad cited Lowy Institute’s report alongside recent reports from Goldman Sachs, the IMF and other international agencies, and lashed out at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for “defaming India in the worst terminology possible” during his foreign visits.
“All these reports are available online. Rahul Gandhi, neither you read yourself nor do those teaching you read,” he charged.
“On what basis are you saying India’s economy has a bleak bleak future and there’s no development in India’s economy?” he asked Mr. Gandhi, adding, “Rahul ji, have you taken a lease to defame India?”

Mr. Prasad alleged that Mr. Gandhi does not follow even the teachings of his great grandfather Jawaharlal Nehru who used to say that there should be a consensus on foreign policy, “especially abroad”.

“Rahul Gandhi, have you even forgotten your family’s values? I will only say, Rahul Gandhi ji, today, you have tarnished the tradition of your family as well. You are seeking to defame the traditions of your own family as far as India’s reputation abroad is concerned,” the former Union Minister charged in an apparent response to Mr. Gandhi’s remarks during his recent U.S. visit.
Mr. Prasad also alleged that Mr. Gandhi is playing into the hands of foreign forces.

India improved its score by 0.5, reaching 40.5, which marks the narrowest gap since 2018 between its score and China’s, which stands at 73.6, as per the Lowy Institute metric

The BJP on Monday (November 23, 2026) claimed that the Congress got a reality check with India’s improved standing in the Lowy Institute’s Asia Power Index 2026, hitting out at the Opposition party over its criticism of the country’s economy and asserting that India was consolidating its position as a “major power” in the region.

India improved its score by 0.5, reaching 40.5, which marks the narrowest gap since 2018 between its score and China’s, which stands at 73.6, as per the Lowy Institute metric.

Its report said India has consolidated its position as the third-most powerful country and a “major powerhouse” in Asia, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi rated as the second-most effective regional leader.

According to the Index, the U.S. and China are “superpowers in Asia for 2026”, with the U.S.’ score being the highest, at 78.9.

Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, senior party leader Ravi Shankar Prasad cited Lowy Institute’s report alongside recent reports from Goldman Sachs, the IMF and other international agencies, and lashed out at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for “defaming India in the worst terminology possible” during his foreign visits.

“All these reports are available online. Rahul Gandhi, neither you read yourself nor do those teaching you read,” he charged.

“On what basis are you saying India’s economy has a bleak bleak future and there’s no development in India’s economy?” he asked Mr. Gandhi, adding, “Rahul ji, have you taken a lease to defame India?”

Mr. Prasad alleged that Mr. Gandhi does not follow even the teachings of his great grandfather Jawaharlal Nehru who used to say that there should be a consensus on foreign policy, “especially abroad”.

“Rahul Gandhi, have you even forgotten your family’s values? I will only say, Rahul Gandhi ji, today, you have tarnished the tradition of your family as well. You are seeking to defame the traditions of your own family as far as India’s reputation abroad is concerned,” the former Union Minister charged in an apparent response to Mr. Gandhi’s remarks during his recent U.S. visit.

Mr. Prasad also alleged that Mr. Gandhi is playing into the hands of foreign forces.

articles.title: High ethanol readings: Suresh Gopi questions sampling process
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: Gopi described the reported ethanol concentrations of 27 and 28 per cent as unacceptable.

Union Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi has challenged Karnataka’s findings of excessive ethanol content in petrol, questioning the methodology used to test fuel samples while defending the Central government’s E20 blending programme.

Addressing the media here on Monday, Mr. Gopi described the reported ethanol concentrations of 27 and 28 per cent as unacceptable. He, however, questioned whether the samples had been collected directly from refineries, noting that petrol undergoes several stages of transportation and storage before reaching consumers.

He pointed out that petrol is transported to retail outlets and stored in underground tanks before being dispensed into vehicles. These stages, he said, must also be taken into account when investigating variations in ethanol content.

The Union Minister maintained that oil companies were responsible for ensuring strict compliance with the Centre’s regulations. He added that periodic inspections were carried out to verify whether fuel met the prescribed quality standards.

Emphasising that the issue should not be politicised, Mr. Gopi said India had international commitments to reduce carbon emissions and transition towards cleaner energy. Ethanol blending, he noted, was an integral part of the country’s broader shift away from fossil fuels towards alternative and more sustainable energy sources.

Citing countries such as Brazil and Paraguay, where ethanol blending levels are higher, he said India could consider increasing the blend to E30 or E40 in the future, subject to scientific assessments and regulatory requirements.

Dismissing concerns over E20 petrol, he said there was no reason for consumers to worry about its use and that people were not being forced to use it. On the Keralam government’s decision to test petrol samples, Mr. Gopi said the State had every right to conduct such tests. He said the Centre had its own test results and would submit them when required, adding that the matter could be examined in court.

fullParagraphs: The Syndicate sub-committee on exams at the University of Calicut (CU) has proposed to reconstitute the boards of examiners who set question papers for the various examinations conducted by the institution every year.

Raveendran, Vice-Chancellor. The university conducts over 15,000 examinations every year. articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: In a note accessed by The Hindu, the Ministry has said that the oil and gas industry has a long gestation period and so exploration and finance decisions taken more than a decade ago are affecting the industry now

The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt.
According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago.

However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration.

“The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.”
The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies.
“Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said.

According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore.

“In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.”
According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

“In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.
These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

The additional capital requirements are intended to enhance the resilience of these institutions.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.

These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision”

Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal.

The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement.

“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

articles.title: Tajikistan becomes fourth country to withdraw from International Criminal Court
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger announced their exits the previous year, ‌denouncing the Court as an instrument of "neocolonial ​repression"

Tajikistan has become the fourth country to ​formally begin withdrawing from the International Criminal Court ‌since the U.S. launched what it called ​a diplomatic push to "dismantle the ⁠court", the Presidency of the Court's governing body said in a statement on Monday (November 23, 2026).

Tajikistan joins Chad, ‌Venezuela and Naoero, a tiny Pacific island nation formerly known as Nauru, which ‌have also announced their withdrawal since the ‌U.S. ⁠called for countries to leave the court ⁠in July.
In March this year, the Court criticised Tajikistan for failing to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin, wanted ​by the ICC for ‌alleged war crimes in Ukraine, when he visited Tajikistan in 2025.
Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger announced their exits the previous year, ‌denouncing the Court as an instrument of "neocolonial ​repression".

The ICC is the world's permanent war crimes tribunal, which prosecutes ⁠individuals accused of genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and the crime of aggression when national courts ‌are unwilling or unable to act.

In a statement published on Monday (November 23, 2026), the Presidency of the ICC's governing body said the move to formally start the one-year process of withdrawing from the ICC risks undermining the collective ‌pursuit of justice and weakens global efforts to end impunity.
​The statement also said the decision to withdraw does not release a state ⁠from obligations incurred while it was still a party ⁠to the treaty.
Currently the ICC has 125 member states but that ‌still includes the seven states that have formally started the withdrawal process, which takes a ​year to complete.

articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: What has changed is that both governments appear increasingly willing to approach security issues through the lens of mutual security interests, rather than allowing these differences to define the entire relationship, says CEO of the Vancouver-based think tank

articles.title: Nepal PM India visit highlights: PM Modi announces offshore campus of IIT in Nepal
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: Establishment of offshore IIT campus in Nepal, scholarships to Nepali students in India, a development package of over ₹15,000 crore for Nepal announced
Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah flag off the ‘Saryu-Kamala Express’ via video conferencing, connecting Ayodhya with Janakpur.

Under the leadership of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, the new direct rail link marks a significant step towards strengthening India-Nepal cultural and religious ties, boosting pilgrimage tourism and facilitating travel for devotees.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted his Nepalese counterpart, Balendra Shah, a Kalamkari Sampoorna Ramayana painting, a Banarasi brocade stole in a Sadeli box, and ‘Gangajal’.
Mr. Modi gifted Mr. Shah the painting, depicting major episodes of Lord Rama’s journey, from his birth and exile to his victory over Ravana and return to Ayodhya, official sources said.

Hand-painted on cotton in the traditional Srikalahasthi style of Andhra Pradesh using a bamboo pen and natural dyes, the artwork showcases India’s rich heritage of storytelling, devotion and traditional craftsmanship.

It also symbolises the enduring spiritual and cultural bond between India and Nepal, connecting Ayodhya, the land of Lord Rama, with Janakpur, revered as the birthplace of Goddess Sita, and reflecting the shared heritage, friendship and values of the two nations.
Nepali PM Balendra Shah called on President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi.

Nepal PM Balen Shah, on an X post said, “With the aim of further strengthening our centuries-old historical relationship and making it relevant to the times, we have held in-depth, meaningful and far-reaching discussions on the many dimensions of our bilateral relations. During these discussions, important agreements on various areas of Nepal–India cooperation were reached, and infrastructure projects were inaugurated and had their foundation stones laid”.

“As a dependable and trusted neighbour, India consistently stood as the first responder in times of natural disasters and difficult times in Nepal,” Nepal PM Balen Shah said, adding that mutual respect, steadfast trust and unbroken goodwill are the bedrock of the relations.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while announcing the Development Cooperation Package of 24,000 crore Nepalese rupees, expressed his condolences over the loss of lives in the Nepal floods.

articles.title: Zelenskyy calls for four-way talks with Russia ‘as soon as possible’
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: During a gathering of Ukrainian supporters in Berlin last week, U.S. envoy Jared Kushner said that Washington might consider offering Ukraine a security guarantee similar to that provided under Article 5 of the North Atlantic Treaty as part of a peace settlement.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (November 23, 2026) called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.
Mr. Zelenskyy, speaking by video to a gathering of lawmakers from NATO countries in Berlin, welcomed the latest push for peace talks with Moscow.
"We must do everything to make sure that the four-party meeting - Ukraine, Europe, America and Russia - happens as soon as possible. We are ready to do this. Literally tomorrow," Mr. Zelenskyy said.
"We have heard from our partners that they want to try to make it happen before Christmas. We hope it happens sooner."
European governments have been excluded from past discussions and their push to join talks has gained prominence in recent weeks.

Mr. Zelenskyy, whose country has been battling a full-scale Russian invasion since February 2022, has repeatedly called for a path to full membership in NATO - and not simply receiving security guarantees from alliance countries.
He argued that Ukraine's combat experience, innovative defence industry and large military would all benefit other allies.
"NATO is the answer - and with a strong Ukrainian army, NATO itself is guaranteed to be stronger," Mr. Zelenskyy told the Berlin gathering.
A number of NATO leaders have expressed hesitation about bringing Ukraine into the alliance.
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte, speaking after Mr. Zelenskyy at the same event on Monday, underscored the alliance's support for Ukraine but noted that joining would require unanimous support.

articles.title: Study finds PTSD-specific brain changes, paving way for personalised treatment
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD

A new study has found that DNA methylation, a natural process that acts like a "dimmer switch" to turn genes down or completely off, varies more than expected across different brain regions in genes linked to PTSD.

Stress and trauma can leave molecular marks in the brain that may help explain the development of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), a mental health disorder in which one experiences flashbacks or nightmares of a terrifying or life-threatening event.

The study, published in the journal ' Cell Reports' , also found that among people affected by PTSD, the molecular variations appeared to be driven by a number of factors, including the sex and race of the person, and whether the trauma exposure occurred in childhood or adulthood.
"The question that our research aims to address is 'What is really different about the PTSD brain?'" corresponding author Frances Champagne of the University of Texas at Austin, US, said.

"The study found greater variation in DNA methylation patterns across brain regions in people with PTSD than in people with major depressive disorder. It also revealed considerable differences among individuals with PTSD," Champagne said.
The findings could open the door to more individualised treatment options for people with PTSD in the future, the researchers said.
A detailed methylation profiling was done of postmortem brains from 302 people -- 101 with PTSD, 100 without psychiatric disorders and 101 with major depressive disorder.

Three different regions of brain were analysed in each sample: the prefrontal cortex, involved in higher level functions, including decision-making, the amygdala or the emotional centre of the brain, and the hippocampus, which manages memory.

The study uncovered specific changes in the brain linked to PTSD, including a relative reduction in oligodendrocytes -- cells that form the protective covering of neurons (myelin sheath) -- in the amygdala of people with PTSD, particularly in those exposed to trauma in adulthood.
PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A new study has found that DNA methylation, a natural process that acts like a "dimmer switch" to turn genes down or completely off, varies more than expected across different brain regions in genes linked to PTSD.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: PTSD was also associated with more pronounced DNA methylation differences in the prefrontal cortex, while major depressive disorder was associated with methylation differences in the amygdala.

articles.title: Rotary Club of Madras partners with Tamil Nadu government to vaccinate 3.5 lakh girls against HPV
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: The club aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29

The Rotary Club of Madras (RCM) and the Tamil Nadu government have entered into a partnership to provide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to 3.5 lakh adolescent girls to prevent cervical cancer.

The partnership, valued at approximately ₹200 crore, is among the largest public-private initiatives for HPV vaccination in India. It was acknowledged in the presence of Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu government.

High-risk HPV infections account for more than 95% of cervical cancer cases. HPV vaccination during adolescence helps prevent infections caused by high-risk HPV types and reduces the risk of cervical cancer later in life.

Bobby Krishna, president of the Rotary Club of Madras, said the partnership was part of Rotary’s efforts to work with the government on large-scale vaccination programmes. The club also aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29, building on its work under the Polio Plus programme.

The club aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29

The Rotary Club of Madras (RCM) and the Tamil Nadu government have entered into a partnership to provide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to 3.5 lakh adolescent girls to prevent cervical cancer.

The partnership, valued at approximately ₹200 crore, is among the largest public-private initiatives for HPV vaccination in India. It was acknowledged in the presence of Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu government.

High-risk HPV infections account for more than 95% of cervical cancer cases. HPV vaccination during adolescence helps prevent infections caused by high-risk HPV types and reduces the risk of cervical cancer later in life.

Bobby Krishna, president of the Rotary Club of Madras, said the partnership was part of Rotary’s efforts to work with the government on large-scale vaccination programmes. The club also aims to vaccinate one million children as it approaches its centenary in 2028-29, building on its work under the Polio Plus programme.

articles.title: Bausch + Lomb's eye-drop drug fails to reduce pain after laser surgery in trial
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & AI Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial

Bausch + Lomb said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study. However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing.

The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), a laser procedure used to correct vision. At six hours after surgery, complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving a placebo.
Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases. The company said there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways.

Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial. Shares of the eye-care company fell 1.4% in extended trading.

Bausch + Lomb said on Thursday its experimental eye-drop treatment failed to show a significant reduction in pain over the first 24 hours after laser eye surgery in a mid-stage study. However, the drug showed signs of benefit in secondary and exploratory analyses, including greater pain relief shortly after surgery and faster corneal healing.

The mid-stage trial tested two doses of BL1332 in 129 patients undergoing photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), a laser procedure used to correct vision. At six hours after surgery, complete pain relief was reported by 14% and 14.6% of patients receiving the two doses, compared with 3.7% of patients receiving a placebo.

Ocular surface pain is a common complication of eye surgery and certain eye diseases. The company said there are currently no approved treatments that directly target its underlying nerve pathways.

Bausch + Lomb said it plans to discuss the results with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration as it considers next steps for the drug, including a potential late-stage trial. Shares of the eye-care company fell 1.4% in extended trading.
